subject: inland taipan
title: The World's Most Venomous Snake Has Never Killed Anyone on Record

scenes.text: One bite from this snake could kill about a hundred people. Its recorded death toll is zero.
The inland taipan has the most toxic venom of any snake ever tested.
One snake's bite can hold enough to kill about two hundred fifty thousand mice.
Yet only a handful of people have ever been bitten, and every one of them survived.
It lives in remote dry plains of inland Australia, and it's shy. It usually slips away.
Most bites came from captive snakes, with antivenom close by. The deadliest venom, with almost nobody near it.

description:
The inland taipan has the most toxic venom of any snake tested, and a single bite can carry enough to kill roughly 100 people or about 250,000 mice.
Yet no human death has been recorded: only a handful of people have been bitten, mostly while handling captive snakes, and all survived with treatment. The snake is shy and lives in remote inland Australia.
Which snake scares you more: the most venomous or the most common?
first_comment: The highest venom yield ever recorded from one inland taipan was 110 mg. Would you ever keep one as a pet?
